scope: Single-vCPU nested-KVM shared-DAX direct handoff; cooperative no concurrent VM ioctl, VMA mutation, IRQFD mutation or eventfd close during transition.
status: passed: source audit, final positive/negative tests, 1000-transfer PIT/churn soak and ordinary KVM regression

residency_review.vmcs_backing: Confirmed in shared arena at offset 0x1d000 after generation 1000; VMCS host fields still refer to native host targets
residency_review.qualification: Source/live read-only review only; no new handoff timing or runtime code changes. Physical L0 nested-KVM VMCS02 and native execution resources are outside the CXL placement scope.

zero_transfer_meaning: No bulk RAM copy or serialized CPU snapshot is sent. Shared-memory writes, CPU cache coherence and VMCS writeback still occur; their traffic is not measured as zero.

data: general registers, RIP/RSP/RFLAGS and control/MSR state
guest RAM and guest page tables
entries.handling: Normal KVM exit/put and VMCLEAR commit processor-resident state into the existing shared objects. Destination resumes those objects. No userspace GET/SET_REGS snapshot roundtrip.

Source writes these values into the shared header. Destination derives its own TSC offset/generation and shifts native timer timestamps from the source anchor to the destination anchor. Values travel through shared memory, not a network serialization format.
entries.note: 56 bytes describes auxiliary fields only, not all execution state or measured CXL traffic.

data: VM identity offsets, RAM HVA/length and creation counters
entries.handling: Release/acquire publication plus compare-exchange; 136-byte ioctl metadata record is currently copied to the shared control mailbox. Many record fields are identity checks or timing diagnostics, rather than essential CPU state.
Source releases hardware ownership; destination installs its own host fields and VPID. Source host values must not be interpreted as destination resources.

data: host page tables for userspace HVA
entries.handling: Destination mm is local. The same fixed HVA must resolve to the same contiguous DAX PFNs; checked before rebinding. Local page metadata is reconnected to shared EPT headers.

data: native PIT worker and hrtimer base
entries.handling: Drain active source observers; reconstruct/reconnect destination-native resources. Existing VM/vCPU FD wrappers can be reused on later visits, but the FD numbers are not transferred.
Handoff is only allowed at a cooperative quiescent boundary. A foreign kernel cannot inherit a native waiter queue. Shared locks must be released before publishing DETACHED.

data: block I/O completion and queue ownership
entries.handling: Not implemented by this prototype. Firecracker control/device runtime stays on A; B uses the existing native executor and limited UART emulation. Shared Rust heap does not transfer epoll, task stacks, or device backend ownership.

new_native_resources: persistent local Firecracker control socket (A only)
new_profiling: Optional 128-byte per-stage timing record at arena offset 512; diagnostic data, not VM execution state.

detach: MMU notifier unregister and reader grace period
PID RCU reader grace period and put_pid
mm reference release and publication preparation
attach: identity/PFN checks and optional FD reservation
native vCPU index and preempt notifier
VM list/PM notifier and optional FD creation

control_profile_parts: DAX ioctl + metadata/logging excluding IRQFD time
source IRQFD removal or destination re-registration
native_wakeup_measurement: Same-kernel CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW: go publication to executor observing go; run_begin is a userspace KVM_RUN attempt, not a hardware first-instruction timestamp.
constraints: Fast control uses one local persistent client and freezes VMM device dispatch during its pause loop; do not mix HTTP commands while that loop is paused.
IRQFD batch supports at most 8 simple IRQFDs; rejects resampling and active IRQ bypass; no concurrent eventfd close or IRQFD modification.
No transfer of active native lock waiters; one VM/vCPU per arena and fixed mappings.
Hardware VMCS compatibility and coherent shared physical addresses are assumptions for future physical multi-host testing.

resume_latency_attribution.status: passed: 9 fresh pairs, 4500 handoffs, 3920 profiled measured samples; CONFIG_KVM_DAX_POOL_TEST=n module build passed

kernel_record.fields: enabled, generation, KVM_RUN and pre-VMX MONOTONIC times, guest-domain TSC/frequency, pair span, diagnostic guest RIP and first VM exit information

resume_latency_attribution.guest_record: 16 appended heartbeat bytes: ACK TSC and epoch; timestamp before release ACK store
resume_latency_attribution.clock_method: destination-local MONOTONIC paired with guest-domain virtual TSC; no cross-node or MONOTONIC_RAW subtraction
resume_latency_attribution.pair_uncertainty: half the bracketing host MONOTONIC sample span; raw negative point estimates retained and verified inside their uncertainty bounds
resume_latency_attribution.semantic_limit: pre-VMX timestamp is an entry attempt, not first guest instruction; post-marker interval includes nested entry and guest execution/exits
resume_latency_attribution.new_host_pointer_state: none; resume profile pointer is destination-local transient kernel stack data pointing into the existing reserved shared arena page

necessity_review.scope: Fresh source purpose/reference audit; native identity vs physical storage; reverse references/tagged IDs; conditional MSR/PMU-filter gaps. No new runtime changes or VM execution tests.
